title: f61's merge-ride is real but measured at ~1.5%: not the suite's floor
description:
The review's named next step for this tick — riding the integrating checkpoint on the merge push (f61's noted follow-up) — is worth roughly 1.5% of a fixture pass: 5 of 62 pushes per pass, pushes being ~19% of active git time. It is still worth doing for production (one fewer push per tick close is one fewer rate slot on the forge), but the measurement says it cannot move A1, and it needs careful design: the held chain would ride a merge commit built on the held tip, with the flush's lease and the merge loop's retry interplay, and the crash-state change (a run killed mid-merge now shows its pre-merge state on origin instead of 'integrating') recorded on its tick. With the write-path cut landed, this is the smallest of the three remaining levers.
evidence: internal/reconcile/integrate.go:44 (the integrating checkpoint before the merge); wrapper profile: 62 pushes per fixture pass at ~40ms each
